newsitem.title: UK: ScotPower says Southern integration ahead.
newsitem.headline: ScotPower says Southern integration ahead.

text.p: British multi-utility Scottish Power Plc said on Thursday that the integration of Southern Water, bought last year, was proceeding well and ahead of published targets on profitability and disposals.

Scottish Power, which said year pretax profits were up 38 percent to 558.4 million pounds ($917.3 million), said it was ahead of target to improve profitability by 52 million pounds a year at Southern and to release 100 million of cash through sell-offs.

"The ScottishPower group is now uniquely placed to exploit the opportunities presented by full liberalisation of the energy markets and this will be our principal focus in the year ahead," chairman Murray Stuart said in a statement.
Scottish Power also owns regional electricity company Manweb and has interests in water, electricity supply and generation as well as gas and telecommunications.

The company, which raised its total dividend payout 19.4 percent to 18.5 pence per share, said it also saw opportunities to make additional savings through management of its Scottish and Manweb energy businesses on a combined basis.

Scottish Power said the year had seen "significant progress" towards its aim of building a multi-utility and said its portfolio of services and strong management "position the group well for the future."
